subject: How to get Table for Figure 6B from your genome biology publication

messages.author: 448686a24ddc1bbb
messages.subject: How to get Table for Figure 6B from your genome biology publication
parts:
Hi,
My name is Nripesh Prasad and i am PhD student at University of Alabama in Huntsville, Huntsville, Alabama, USA. I have been using methylkit package in R for RRBS data analysis. I am very impressed by this package.
Since i am new to this package, can you please let me know how can i get a list of table of entries for Figure 6B in your publication, i am able to plot the pie chart but i need data that is used to plot this pie chart. especially Differentially methylated CpGs in promoter region of this pie chart. Here is what i am doing

# Calculate differential methylation p-values and q-values
myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth)
head(myDiff)
write.table(myDiff, "C:\\Users\\xxxx\\Documents\\xxxx\\xxxx\\myDiff.txt", sep="\t")

# PLOT Hypo and Hyper methylated regions per chromosome
diffMethPerChr(myDiff, plot = TRUE, qvalue.cutoff = 0.01, meth.cutoff = 25, legend.text = TRUE, args.legend = list(x = "bottomright", bty = "n", inset=c(-0.15, 0)))


#Annotate differentially methylated bases/regions read-in transcript locations to be used in annotation
# IMPORTANT: annotation files that come with the package (version >=0.5) are a subset of full annotation
# files. Download appropriate annotation files from UCSC (or other sources) in BED format
gene.obj=read.transcript.features ("C:\\Users\\xxxx\\Documents\\xxxx\\xxxx\\rn4.refseq.bed.txt")

# Annotate differentially methylated Cs with promoter/exon/intron using annotation data
annotate.WithGenicParts(myDiff25p,gene.obj)


This is the result i get:

summary of target set annotation with genic parts
18313 rows in target set
--------------
--------------
percentage of target features overlapping with annotation :
  promoter       exon     intron intergenic 
  10.91028   14.61803   26.51122   55.66537 


percentage of target features overlapping with annotation (with promoter>exon>intron precedence) :
  promoter       exon     intron intergenic 
  10.91028   10.33692   23.08742   55.66537 


percentage of annotation boundaries with feature overlap :
promoter     exon   intron 
8.221964 1.050970 2.265220 


summary of distances to the nearest TSS :
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
      0    6864   31200  106100  103000 7384000 

But when i am typing :
write.table(annotate.WithGenicParts, "C:\\Users\\xxxx\\Documents\\xxxx\\xxxx\\annotate.WithGenicParts.txt", sep="\t")

I get the following error:

Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) : 
  cannot coerce class "structure("standardGeneric", package = "methods")" to a data.frame


However, when i am typing:

# plot nearest distance to TSS
tss.assoc=getAssociationWithTSS(diffAnn)
write.table(tss.assoc, "C:\\Users\\xxxx\\Documents\\xxxx\\xxxx\\tss.assoc.txt", sep="\t")

I am able to export the tss.accoc.txt file


Question: How can i export the list of the % differentially methylated CpGs in promoter, exon, intron, intergenic regions (highlited in red above) as .txt file.


Thanks
Nripesh

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: How to get Table for Figure 6B from your genome biology publication
parts:
Hi,
You can get that vector using @ notation which accesses different slots in the object (S4 objects in R).

x=annotate.WithGenicParts(myDiff25p,gene.obj)
vec=x@annotation

df=as.data.frame(vec)

# now you can write out the result using write.table()



Best,
ALtuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: How to get Table for Figure 6B from your genome biology publication
parts:
you can use getMembers(x) which will return overlap status of each CpG with the annotation as a matrix. 1 for CpGs overlapping with annotation, 0 for a non-overlap. You can use that matrix to subset the methylDiff object.

ann.mat=getMembers(x)
head(ann.mat)

# promoter overlapping CpGs
myDiff25p[ann.mat[,1]==1,]

# exon overlapping CpGs
myDiff25p[ann.mat[,2]==1,]

# intron overlapping CpGs
myDiff25p[ann.mat[,3]==1,]



Best,
Altuna
